posts.caption: C5.9 one-page: the eight steps, the one record, and why no customer data is reachable
posts.comment:
Asked: give a prospect a safe, honest way to see the platform working without a live customer tenant. Sample data labeled on every screen, no real customer data reachable, the route verified mounted, and a PR open rather than merged.
Delivered: the guided walkthrough at /demo, now merged, deployed and prod-verified, with both artifacts attached.

Takeaway: "no real customer data reachable" is a property of the module graph, not a promise in a review. The page imports no API client, so it cannot reach the backend at all. The build reads the import list from disk and fails if one ever appears. Every public page on this site already renders from constants and fetches nothing, so this is the established pattern rather than a shortcut: a page that cannot reach the backend cannot leak a tenant.

Sample data is labeled on every screen because the badge lives inside the per-step component. It cannot be present on some steps and missing on others. That detail matters more than it sounds: a single banner at the top scrolls away, and a screenshot of step four would then be indistinguishable from a real customer board.

Eight steps, one record. STORY-1042 goes from unverified, to matched against commit a3f91c2, to verified with 3 of 3 criteria checked. It is defined once and referenced fifteen times rather than repeated, so the steps cannot drift from the record they describe.

posts.caption: C5.9 the full spec: each criterion, the evidence behind it, and the three deliberate departures
posts.comment:
The full document: every acceptance criterion with the evidence behind it, the eight steps, the three deliberate departures from the C4.4 storyboard, and what the page says it is not.

Three departures, all deliberate. The storyboard uses seven real frames and one sample; here every step is sample, because there is no live tenant behind a public page and showing a real learner's project to the open internet is not something we may do. No figure from the narration appears, because those counts have no claim-registry row: they are true of our database and fine on a call where you can date them. And it does not mock the product interface, because a faithful fake board is the exact defect the sample badge was written against.

Three of the five build guards were wrong on their first attempt, and the document says so. One counted badges in source when the badge sits inside a map, so a correct page scored one badge for eight steps. One matched the comment explaining why a figure is excluded. One counted a literal string when the page correctly references a constant, so the right pattern scored one and a worse one would have passed. Each would have produced a confident and false artifact, which is the reason to break a guard before trusting it.

Production: https://enterprise.colaberry.ai/demo - public, no auth, no feature flag. Verified in the served bundle both ways: strings from this page present, strings from the replaced page absent. On a single-page app a status code proves nothing, because a path that never existed also returns 200.

PR: https://github.com/ColaberryIntern/ColaberryEnterprise_AI_LeadershipAccelerator/pull/3252 (merged)
